decisions.decision: A1 is answered by a LOCAL harness, with no source change and no CI cycle
decisions.rationale: server.ts:128-133 answers a read-only PUT with 403 and RETURNS BEFORE calling handlePut, so no backend method runs on a refused PUT and the backend's identity provably cannot affect the PUT path. That makes the existing createReadOnlyMemoryBackend exactly equivalent for this question, and it is PUT-maximal because it is permanently empty so every task must execute. Verified independently by the orchestrator.

server.ts has ZERO @actions/* imports and is deliberately GitHub-agnostic, and it backs createCacheServer which is the ENTIRE EXPECTED_VALUE_EXPORTS (public-surface.spec.ts:40). Adding @actions/core there would make the package's only public value export transitively depend on an Actions-only package for consumers outside Actions. This was the orchestrator's original design and it was a defect.

decisions.decision: No permanent test or standing guard added
decisions.rationale: The durable half (PUT -> 403) is our code and is already covered at that branch (server.spec.ts:359). The new half (does the Nx client attempt a store) is THIRD-PARTY behaviour -- guarding it would test Nx and redden on an unrelated bump. The failure mode it would catch is also self-announcing.

Always count tap lines added by the run before believing a silence.
